page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.e3.large is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz. It features 4 dedicated physical cores with 1 thread per core, providing 4 vCPUs. The instance is configured with 32.0 GB of RAM, yielding an 8.0 GB memory-to-core ratio. It does not include any local storage or GPU hardware, relying on network-attached storage for its operating system and data.

Benchmark evaluations indicate that the ecs.e3.large exhibits modest processing capabilities. In stress-ng and Geekbench testing, both single-core and multi-core CPU performances fall into the bottom 25% tier. Similarly, single-threaded gzip and bzip3 decompression speeds are positioned in the bottom 10%. While memory read bandwidth is relatively weak, the large-block memory write bandwidth achieves an average rating in the middle 50% tier. Passmark CPU extended instructions also reach average performance levels, though database operations and Redis SET operations remain in the lower percentiles.

The primary tradeoff of the ecs.e3.large is its high memory-to-vCPU ratio paired with lower-tier compute performance. This configuration offers a qualitative cost advantage for memory-bound workloads that do not require intense CPU throughput, as users avoid paying for high-performance compute cores to obtain 32 GB of RAM. Suitable workloads include caching layers, lightweight database nodes, memory-intensive utility scripts, and general-purpose applications with low CPU utilization but moderate memory footprints.
